items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: I was auditioning for Johnny Benson

ctx.x: Can we stop and say, Gierkowski was from Mississippi, but he lived here in New Orleans, and recorded probably one of the, uh, most popular songs in rhythm and blues in 1954, was called Things I Used to Do, and Earl, and Gierkowski and them were very good friends at that time.

Yeah, well, um, Slim was recording at the time for the specialty records. Uh, I was auditioning for Johnny Benson, and Earl was a speciality, and as people were, as soon as the hit pops up, everybody wants to appreciate it. You know, just, hey, get on the bandwagon, let's cut something like that. But we didn't take into fact what you wanted to do musically, just get on the door, right, and go that direction to the bandwagon. Uh, we did some things that were on the line of the things I used to do. And, um, after…
I met someone, I felt in love, after what I heard. And I was sorry, even I left well, and I wasn't alone. This is how it sounded in 1953.
